Chapter 2: Identifying What Matters Most—Core Priorities and Values
So, now that you can actually see where your week’s hours go, let’s talk about what really deserves a spot in your schedule.
You know, most of us end up filling our calendars on autopilot—just reacting to requests, obligations, and old routines without ever stopping to ask, “What matters to me, really?”
But here’s the thing—true fulfillment comes when you line up your time with what you value most and those big-picture goals that light you up.
How do you figure out what those things are? It starts with a little reflection.
Picture this: you’re looking back at your week, and you feel genuinely proud of how you spent your time. What did you do? Who did you connect with? What did you achieve?
Those are your core priorities. They’re the activities and relationships that give your days meaning, satisfaction, and a real sense of progress.
For one person, that might mean spending quality time with family, making strides at work, or volunteering in the community. For someone else, it could be diving into creative projects, learning something new, or focusing on health.
If you want a clearer picture, here’s a quick exercise you can try:
Start by listing out the roles you play in life—like parent, professional, friend, or volunteer.
Then, for each role, jot down what an “ideal week” would look like.
Finally, pick out the top two or three areas that—if you gave them more attention—would make your life feel richer.
Remember, this isn’t about sketching out a fantasy schedule. It’s about bringing to the surface what truly matters to you.
And honestly, the gap between your current routine and your ideal isn’t always as big as it seems.
Sometimes, just small tweaks in how you spend your time can make a huge difference in how satisfied you feel.
Once you’re clear on your priorities, it’s time to see how your actual week lines up.
That time log you kept? It’s like a mirror, showing you whether your hours are backing up your values—or pulling you away from them.
And you might notice that a lot of your time goes to things that don’t even make the priority list—like meetings that drag on, chores that eat up your energy, or social commitments that leave you feeling drained.
But don’t beat yourself up. This isn’t about blame—it’s just a side effect of living in a world that’s constantly throwing demands your way.
The real trick is to get intentional. Start choosing to put more time into your core priorities, and less into those lower-value activities. Pretty soon, your week will start to look—and feel—a lot more like the life you want.
A few simple strategies can really help here:
First, schedule your most important activities first, and treat them like non-negotiable appointments.
Next, try bundling similar tasks together to cut down on switching gears—and that nagging mental clutter.
And maybe the hardest part: get comfortable saying no, or at least renegotiating commitments that don’t fit with your values.
The point here isn’t to get everything perfect. It’s about making progress.
Even just spending a bit more time on what matters most can totally change how you feel about your week.
So, the real goal? Move from a life where you’re just reacting by default, to one where you’re designing your days around what’s most important to you—your deepest values and biggest ambitions.
